evidence: At file 6C0Fh the target loads offset 9E27h before scanning environment entries; 25E0h + 9E27h points to COPYCMD=.

observations: Target routine at 6B33h checks destination attributes with INT 21h AX=4300h and presents a choice through the message service.

The input loop reads characters through INT 21h AH=0Ch/AL=08h, compares three response characters after DOS uppercase conversion, and returns carry for one response; the third accepted response clears the overwrite-confirmation flag.
The environment routine at 6C00h searches COPYCMD=, scans for /Y, and adjusts the same flag; a fallback checks a resident-state word.
At 6C73h target code resumes with the same instruction structure as the next reference module at 67F4h, supporting the identified added-routine boundary.

observations: The call at 6B7Eh and the later call at 6BE4h share the same target at file offset 8091h.
The target entry matches the first eight bytes of reference SYSDISPMSG; its reference offset is independently derived from the tprintf listing and link map.
The target passes message numbers 044Fh and 042Eh respectively, and builds an 11-byte substitution block containing the destination path.
These observations identify the historical message-service interface; exact message definitions and target placement remain unresolved.
The target message stores the permitted response bytes Y, N and A immediately after the prompt.
After DOS case conversion, Y returns with carry clear; N returns with carry set; A clears the overwrite-confirmation flag and returns with carry clear.
The 11-byte runtime substitution block uses the existing Microsoft $M_SUBLIST_STRUC layout and points to DestBuf.
This identifies behavior and structure, but source symbol names and all cross-file definitions remain unproven.

evidence: The COPYCMD fallback compares the target RESGROUP word at 02C5h with zero.
At corresponding file positions, the target has five bytes 63 6F 78 00 00 before the reference data resumes; the tested word lies in the last two inserted bytes.
This indicates a target-specific resident-data dependency, rather than a safely identifiable existing reference symbol.
resident_fallback_dependency.limitations: The observed batch, single-command and interactive paths are established; other command sources, original symbol name and integration remain unverified. Later source files are not modified out of order.
observations: The target copies UCOMBUF to COMBUF, emits CRLF, clears AX, and writes AX into RESGROUP:02C5h.
An alternate entry emits CRLF, sets AX to one, and joins the same write.

The existing tcode.asm source has analogous interactive input and DOCOM/DOCOM1 paths, so the state appears to distinguish the origin of the command; exact coverage of the alternate path remains to be verified.
The batch-read completion at 2873h and the single-command buffer path at 2899h both jump directly to 28D4h, which loads AX=1 before storing the resident word.
The interactive input path instead loads AX=0; with COPYCMD absent, COPY reads that word to decide whether to suppress overwrite confirmation.
